# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

reasoning:
As Carol, the Vanilla Villager, I'm weighing Grace's trial with the competing claims — Heidi says Surveyor, Grace says Medic, Erin also says Medic. I'm also noting Judy's archive pool of roles and Frank's claim about Puppeteer writing Day 3 messages, which suggests a Puppeteer is active among us.

I'm comparing Grace's and Erin's Medic claims closely: both say they protected Carol N1 and Frank N2, but diverge on N3 (Heidi vs. Frank). Erin's token count and the Day 4 "no deaths" announcement make me suspicious about who actually saved Frank from the N3 Katana attack and whether Frank's claim about not writing his own Day 3 messages holds up.

Both Medics claim protecting Carol on N1, but only one can be real, and both also claim protecting Frank N2, which is another overlap worth tracking. Carol was the Katana target N1 and survived, so whichever Medic's claim checks out there is likely genuine, and I should see how Grace's claim of protecting Heidi N3 fits against Heidi's own statements.

Comparing Frank's Scout N3 report (Alice, Grace, Ivan separate) against Grace's claim of visiting Heidi and Heidi's claim of visiting Alice creates a contradiction — under Grace's story, Alice-Heidi-Grace form one group, but Frank says Alice and Grace are separate. The simplest resolution is that Grace is lying (matching Erin's accusation), which would leave Alice-Heidi together and Grace alone, consistent with Frank's report, provided Heidi's survey claim holds.

I also want to check whether a Surveyor's survey action counts as a "visit" for grouping purposes, and look at Bob's Clerk claim against Heidi's broader group analysis.

Now I'm focused on identifying the Yakuza. Judy's dead and was Archivist, not Yakuza, and there's a confirmed Puppeteer who hijacked Frank on Day 3 — meaning the pushes against Grace and Heidi that appeared to come from Frank that day likely weren't actually his words, which changes how I should weigh those earlier accusations.

It's ambiguous whether the puppeteer attacking Grace and Heidi through "Frank" was meant to frame Frank or shield Grace/Heidi, which makes me uncertain about their alignment. I'm also recalling Grace's Day 1 comment defending Carol's nudge on Mallory as not necessarily malicious.

Tracing the thread further, Grace and Heidi both pushed back against Frank turning on Carol, and Ivan sided with them too, while Dave's Day 3 nomination of Frank shows he's been suspicious of him from early on — this cluster of defenders makes me weigh whether Grace, Erin, or Carol fit a scum profile given inconsistencies in their claims about Frank being targeted on N2 and N3.

Both Grace and Erin claim to have protected Carol N1, which means one of them is lying about being the real Medic, and both also claim to have protected Frank N2 even though Judy was the actual Katana target that night — suggesting the real Medic guessed wrong on Frank. For N3, Heidi's Day 4 statement that she was the actual target Grace saved fits with Grace's claim and would explain the pattern of zero kills on N1 and N3.

Checking the seating arrangement confirms Carol's neighbors are Bob and Dave, and Frank's neighbors are Erin and Grace, which lines up consistently. Now I'm weighing who might be the Yakuza, noting that Erin has been notably defensive of Frank's Scout claim.

Grace attacked Frank heavily on Day 3, which stands out alongside the puppeteer messages. With Grace currently on trial and no clear alignment read on myself as Vanilla, I'm tracing Bob's Clerk claim and his voting history on Carol and Dave's nominations, trying to figure out whether the rigged day actually lines up with Dave's failed nomination on Day 4.

Tracing the group logic from Heidi's claim: the Clerk must be either Bob or Dave in one group and Mallory or Bob in another, and since Alice, Carol, and Dave all deny being Clerk, Bob emerges as the only consistent candidate if Heidi is honest — which would make Bob the Clerk, and therefore likely Yakuza since that's the Clerk's alignment.

Looking at Heidi and Grace's relationship, they seem mutually supportive — Grace's Medic claim backs up Heidi's survey result, which places the Medic somewhere in Erin, Frank, or Grace. If Heidi's Surveyor claim is genuine and Frank really is the Scout he claims to be, then the Medic narrows down to either Erin or Grace, both of whom have made claims that could fit.

Since two people can't both be the real Medic, one is lying, and I'm trying to figure out which. Both Erin and Grace claim to have saved Carol on the first night, but since Carol's attack was publicly known, that's an easy detail for a fake Medic to copy, so it doesn't help distinguish them. Now I'm turning to Erin's second claim about protecting Frank — since Frank wasn't actually attacked that night as the Scout, this protection claim doesn't line up cleanly, which makes me suspicious of her story.

Frank's correction muddies things though — he claims the Puppeteer wrote his N2 message, not him, so that report may be fake regardless. Checking Heidi's N3 survey on Alice confirms the Heidi-Alice link, which supports Grace lying and Erin being the real Medic, since Frank's N3 group report would otherwise be contradicted if Grace were truthful.

Heidi being honest fits too — her protection claim aligns with Erin's version where Frank was the N3 target, meaning Heidi wasn't attacked. So I'm leaning toward Grace being the one lying here.

But I'm wary of voting Guilty immediately since my plan was to wait until things resolve further. The core tension is Frank's N3 Scout claim plus Erin's consistent account versus Grace's conflicting N3 visit claim, and whether Frank would've mentioned being attacked if he actually was the target — his silence on it is ambiguous. I'm also weighing Grace's N1 claim about protecting Carol, since Carol would know directly whether that's true.

Thinking about Frank's clarification that his Day 3 pushes on Grace and Heidi weren't actually his own messages but puppeted ones — that's odd, since a Yakuza puppeteer attacking Grace and Heidi as "defenders of Carol's prompt" doesn't obviously benefit Yakuza unless the goal was to generate sympathy for Grace or Heidi by making it look like Frank was targeting them unfairly.

As Carol, I'm thinking about whether to speak this turn given my remaining budget. The key point worth raising is that Frank's Night 3 scout result separating Alice, Grace, and Ivan is the one independent visit fact, and it actually conflicts with Grace's claim that she visited Heidi while Heidi visited Alice.

So either Grace or Heidi is lying, and since Heidi's Surveyor claim fits the archive pool and the clerk logic, Grace looks like the likely liar — unless Erin is secretly Yakuza and using a fake Medic claim to frame Grace, or Frank himself is Yakuza falsifying the scout result. I lean toward trusting Frank's N3 result as genuine, which points suspicion squarely at Grace.

Given Frank and Erin's stories hold together, Grace looks like the Yakuza liar, so I'm leaning toward a Guilty vote on Grace — though Heidi's claim about Grace's N3 protection creates some tension with that theory that I need to weigh.

Grace's swap excuse would itself require a Smuggler to actually be used, which is a stretch. With the trial vote coming up, I need to decide whether speaking is worth the budget cost given I have 2.0 free.

I'll draft a concise public message of around 80 words stating my vote and reasoning, leaving notepad, claim, and last_will empty since they don't apply here.

Erin's Medic story fits that Scout result and explains Frank's N3 survival; Grace's doesn't. Grace, if the Smuggler swapped visits, name it and say how."

But wait, Heidi's claim hasn't actually been shown false yet.

answers.confusing_rules: The Day 1 night results are labelled 'Day 1 night' but are announced at the start of Day 2, and the Night 1 and Night 2 Yakuza results sit under different Day labels, so it took effort to match each night to its events. The Surveyor and Diviner group rules ('plus nearest neighbours, skipping yourself, never counting anyone twice') were hard to apply to a circle after deaths removed players. The Puppeteer rule ('chat publicly and privately in their place') does not say whether the puppet's own private messages are shown to anyone, so the 'sent a private message' ledger felt incomplete. The Arsonist's ignite versus douse timing (doused on one night, ignited later, ignition kills every doused player at once) was not clearly stated in R9 or R20.
answers.missing_information: I could not see my remaining speaking budget, the round multiplier or the price table in the prompts I received, so I could not plan message length or count what I could afford. I also had no compact visit-graph view: linking Surveyor groups, Scout groups, protections and Katana visits across several nights by hand was error-prone. The notepad limit of 375 words is tight for 11 players across 5 nights. Per-night role-block status and whether a Yakuza's Katana vote was tied or missing were not shown explicitly.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As a dead Yakuza I had no way to see, in a single place, which teammates' private messages were already sent to the other side, so I could not check whether Ivan and Bob were leaking. I wanted to ask Bob directly, in a private day message, whether his Clerk token was still unused before the nomination vote, but team plans and day PMs are discouraged by the strategy rules, so I could not coordinate that safely. I could not see the Day 5 turn history of the last nominations while deciding my own last-will text, which I wanted to tailor to the visit-graph conflicts that decided the endgame.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Death reveals sometimes showed the role and sometimes not: Heidi's and Frank's last wills stated their roles, and Erin's last will named her Medic role, which seems to conflict with the setting that hides roles. Mallory's Night 1 result said she doused Dave, and Dave's death on Night 4 was counted as an ignition, which is consistent, but the public death list did not explain that Dave's death was linked to a doused player. Heidi's Night 4 result said she had no action while her Night 4 target line was never filled in, and the Night 3 Erin protection entry appeared in both Erin's and Grace's accounts, which made the public record confusing. The Cardinal's curse on Frank was attributed to Dave's death without stating which night's end the divine attack happened on.
answers.suggestions: Show the speaking budget, round multiplier and price table in every turn prompt, as the rules describe. Add a short per-night visit list (who visited whom, with Katana and Arsonist visits marked) to the public ledger so visit-graph contradictions can be checked without manual tracing. Label each night's results with the night number rather than the following Day. State in the rules whether a puppet's private messages are visible to the puppeteer's team and whether private-message counts include the puppeted player. Raise the notepad limit or allow a longer summary field, since 11 players and 5 nights overflow 375 words.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Cardinal vs. Jester revenge ordering on Night 4. Dave (Cardinal) died to the Arsonist on the same night Grace's Jester revenge was due. I read 'after all of that night's other actions and attacks' as meaning the curse is drawn only after the revenge has resolved. So Erin, already killed by the revenge, was excluded, and Frank was drawn from Carol and Frank. The rules never explicitly rank these two deferred Astral attacks against each other. 2) R6 self-targeting Medic (Erin, Night 4): the Medic 'can target others', so a self-protect 'shows as visiting themself'. For the Cartographer and Scout, a self-visit links no one. I treated Erin as a singleton group. That works, but the interplay of R6, the Fortune Teller's self-visit counting and the Scout/Cartographer graph rules took cross-referencing to apply. 3) It is unclear whether a Puppeteer's puppet action is a visit. I treated it as a visit under the default (Ivan to Frank, Night 2). Frank's Scout result came out the same either way, but the Puppeteer text doesn't say. 4) Executioner to Jester conversion timing: Grace's target Judy died on Night 2, and I notified Grace at the start of Day 3. The rules don't say when the conversion notice is delivered.

I also wanted a way to send the attacked-by notices for deferred attacks: there is no logged private message telling Erin she was killed by Jester revenge or Frank that the Cardinal's curse killed him, which R3 calls for.

This contradicts the announced order. 2) Under the no-role-reveal setting, the public causes of death 'killed by Jester's revenge' and 'killed by Cardinal's curse' effectively revealed hidden roles. Grace was the only player hanged, so 'Jester's revenge' outs her as Jester. 'Cardinal's curse' outs a Cardinal among the night's dead. That partly defeats the setting. 3) As noted above, Erin and Frank received no private attack notifications for their Night 4 deaths. 4) Bob's Night 4 message bundled 'You died' with 'Your Katana attack on Heidi succeeded'. This is correct under R10 (simultaneous resolution), but it reads oddly. 5) Every other result I checked matched the rules: the Archivist sample, all of Heidi's Surveyor groups, all of Frank's Scout groups (Nights 1–4), the Katana pass to Ivan, and the final win (Mallory as Arsonist alone, Grace as Jester for being hanged).

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's lone Innocent on Grace's trial was futile and Bob was later killed; the team's vote math mattered, though the Yakuza ended up with the Arsonist winning rather than the Village.

tips_feedback.tip: Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails.
tips_feedback.why: The Day 5 PM exchange between Ivan and Carol was the public basis that got Ivan hanged, and it also let the surviving players spot the coordination.

tips_feedback.tip: A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's Katana survival and Grace's Medic-style protection story were both unverifiable, and surviving a Katana hit can come from innate Defense or a protector who isn't yet claimed, so survival alone is weak evidence.

lessons.tip: Treat anonymous role samples and Surveyor results as possibilities, not player identifications. Two groups reporting the same role do not show that the same person has it; roles can repeat, and Judy’s archive sample was incomplete.

A mechanical contradiction can show that at least one account is false without identifying which player is evil. Before pushing a hang, consider whether the liar could be a Jester who benefits from execution, and avoid turning a contradiction into certainty about faction.

lessons.applies_to: Village players voting on a possible Jester
lessons.tip: If a hang is necessary but a Jester is plausible, seek only the Guilty votes needed and keep likely power roles off the Guilty side when possible: a Jester’s revenge can kill a random Guilty voter.

Weigh the value of revealing a role and its full information against making yourself an obvious night target or handing opponents a ready-made fake-claim list. Share information deliberately, and preserve a clear record in your will.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar.
tips_feedback.why: A partial archive is a random sample, not a census, and Surveyor reports one randomly selected role from a group without identifying its holder. Roles may repeat unless marked Unique, so a role appearing once in either result does not establish a single holder.

tips_feedback.tip: A contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang.
tips_feedback.why: This distinction was crucial: Grace’s false Medic claim and the visit-graph conflict made her look like a liar, but she was a Jester and won when the table executed her. The contradiction exposed a false claim, not a Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side.
tips_feedback.why: Nine players voted Guilty on Grace, including Erin, the real Medic. The Jester’s revenge then killed a random Guilty voter, Erin. The broad Guilty vote gave the revenge a valuable target.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonists who keep dousing should ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment they are suspected.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited after dousing three living players. The attack killed Alice, Bob, and Dave, including two Yakuza, and helped secure the endgame.

lessons.tip: Plan douses as a set, not as isolated actions: prioritize targets likely to be valuable or share a faction, keep the running list accurate, and ignite when the simultaneous hit is decisive. Waiting until several players are doused can turn one action into a major swing.

Separate “these reports cannot all be true” from “this person is Evil.” A mechanical contradiction identifies a false claim or result, not necessarily its faction; consider Jester and Executioner incentives before voting to hang.
Keep a cover claim narrow and consistent with public facts, and make accusers compare it with their own unverified claims. Don’t invent extra results that create new ways to be checked.
In a multi-faction endgame, evaluate the consequences of a hang as well as the case for it. A vote can remove a dangerous opponent and still hand a Jester an independent win.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory doused three players by Night 3 and ignited on Night 4, killing Alice and Bob, both Yakuza, as well as Dave. The simultaneous attack removed the rival faction’s power and made the eventual Arsonist win possible.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory correctly pointed out that Heidi’s two Surveyor results showing Clerk in overlapping groups did not prove Bob was the only possible Clerk: each result names a random group member, and roles can repeat. That prevented an unsupported conclusion about Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang.
tips_feedback.why: The Day 4 visit-graph conflict was real, but it did not establish Grace’s faction. Grace was a Jester by then and won when executed; treating the contradiction as enough to hang her overlooked the tip’s warning.

tips_feedback.tip: Village: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: After Ivan died, Carol correctly reasoned that the game continuing was inconsistent with both her Vanilla claim and Mallory’s claimed Village alignment. That exposed Mallory as non-Village, although the two-player voting threshold kept Carol from executing her.

summary: Mallory (Arsonist) won alone. Grace (Executioner, turned Jester when her target Judy died to the Katana on N2) also won by getting hanged. The Yakuza (Alice, Bob, Ivan) controlled the Katana all game but made weak use of their tokens. Ivan spent the puppet on Frank to post a fake N2 Scout result. On Day 4 Frank exposed it, which confirmed a Puppeteer existed. Bob never used his rig and then openly admitted Clerk after Heidi's survey math (N1 and N3 groups both showed Clerk and overlapped only on Bob). Village should have hanged Bob on Day 4. Instead Grace fake-claimed Medic, and Erin counterclaimed with a full log. Frank's N3 Scout groups showed Grace's claimed visit was false, so the town hanged Grace 9-1 without asking whether she was a Jester. Erin, the real Medic, voted Guilty with everyone else. Night 4 was decisive. Mallory had quietly doused Dave, Alice and Bob, then ignited and killed all three, including the Katana holder Bob and Dave the hidden Cardinal. The Katana killed Heidi. Grace's Jester revenge killed Erin, and Dave's Cardinal curse killed Frank. Six people died in one night. That left Carol (Vanilla), Ivan (Yakuza) and Mallory, a position Carol could not win: hanging either opponent hands the game to the other. Carol and Mallory hanged Ivan, and Mallory ignited Carol on N6. Nobody ever seriously suspected the Arsonist, even though Judy's archive listed one and Mallory admitted on Day 2 that she had 'taken an action elsewhere'.

lessons.tip: When a Yakuza has effectively confirmed themself, hang them before a contested claimer. A player whose fake claim breaks against mechanics may be a Jester, or an Executioner who became one, and hanging them gives them the win plus a Divine revenge kill. If you do hang a possible Jester, keep it to a bare majority and keep your confirmed power roles on Innocent.
lessons.evidence: On Day 4 Bob had admitted Clerk and both of Heidi's surveys pointed at him, yet the town hanged Grace 9-1. Grace was a Jester; her revenge picked Erin, the real Medic, from the Guilty voters, and Grace won.

lessons.tip: Track the conversion chain. If an archive lists Executioner and a quiet player dies to the Katana, assume a Jester may now exist. Look hard at sudden power-role claims that seem designed to get their speaker hanged.
lessons.evidence: Judy's archive showed Executioner. Judy (Grace's target) died to the Katana on N2. On Day 4 Grace jumped onto Heidi's 'Medic in {Erin, Frank, Grace}' result with a claim that was easy to disprove, and nobody raised the Jester possibility.

lessons.tip: If a Neutral killing role (Arsonist or Serial Killer) appears in an archive or survey, give each player a slot. Press anyone who admits a night action but won't name a role or target. Arsonists douse silently and then wipe out several players at once.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 Mallory said 'I took an action elsewhere' while the archive listed Arsonist, and nobody followed up. On N4 her ignite killed Alice, Bob and Dave, and the knock-on effects left Village unable to win.

lessons.tip: Douse quietly across several nights, spreading your douses over different suspects. Ignite once 3+ players are doused, ideally just before the Yakuza and town finish each other off. Prepare a fake claim that explains your visits (Ex-Con fits well).
lessons.evidence: Mallory doused Dave, Alice and Bob on N1-N3 and ignited on N4, killing the Katana holder and the Cardinal. On Day 5 her Ex-Con claim got Carol to vote Innocent on her and then to hang Ivan with her.

lessons.tip: Don't use a puppet to post fake investigative results for a living investigator. They will correct it the next Day, which proves a Puppeteer exists and makes their real results look stronger. Use the puppet for something that can't be undone, such as a damaging nomination or vote push, or on a player the town is about to hang.
lessons.evidence: Ivan posted a fake N2 Scout result as Frank. On Day 4 Frank posted the real one and the town took it as confirmation of the Puppeteer from Judy's archive. Frank's results then drove Grace's hanging.

lessons.tip: When an investigation only probabilistically points at you, keep up the ambiguity your teammates have built ('roles repeat, the sample could be different players'). Never publicly confirm an Evil role. Spend one-shot tokens like the rig before you are exposed.
lessons.evidence: Ivan, Mallory and Dave had already argued that Heidi's overlap didn't prove Bob was Clerk. Bob then claimed Clerk outright. He died on N4 with his rig token unused.

lessons.tip: When a fake Medic claims your role, counterclaim at once with your full nightly log and check it against attacks and survivals. A claimed Medic whose targets don't explain a known survival is the one to doubt.
lessons.evidence: Erin's log (Carol N1, Frank N2, Frank N3) explained Frank surviving the N3 Katana attack and Frank's Scout groups. That exposed Grace's false Medic claim, although Erin should not then have voted Guilty herself.

lessons.tip: At three alive with two hidden enemy factions, a lone Villager usually can't win. Spend Days 3-4 identifying every faction so you don't reach that endgame. Before a mass-death night, work out what pending curses (Cardinal, Jester) will cost.
lessons.evidence: Carol faced Ivan (Yakuza) and Mallory (Arsonist) on Day 5. Hanging either one gave the game to the other, so no choice could save her.

tips_feedback.tip: If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it: Grace (Jester) was hanged 9-1 and her revenge killed Erin, the real Medic. Following this tip would have kept Erin alive or avoided giving Grace the win.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction... Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang.
tips_feedback.why: Players named the contradiction between Frank's N3 groups and Grace's claimed visit, but nobody used the Jester caveat. Grace's deliberately broken claim was exactly the Jester case the tip warns about.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited as soon as she had three douses (Dave, Alice, Bob). That killed three players including the Katana holder and set up her solo win.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi combined Judy's archive with her survey groups to isolate Bob as Clerk, and Bob then admitted it.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted.
tips_feedback.why: Bob kept saving his rig 'for a decisive day' every night and died on N4 with it unused. The puppet was spent early on fake results that backfired. Ivan holding his puppet token on N1 for a 'better' day had no payoff either.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: Erin self-protected on N4 as advised, which left Heidi unprotected against the Katana. Erin died anyway to the Divine Jester revenge, which no protection can stop.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored the Arsonist until it was too late, despite the archive and Mallory's 'action elsewhere'. On Day 5 Carol did keep Mallory in the pool, but by then the position was lost.

issues.description: Day 1: repeated HTTP 429 rate-limit errors made Mallory's first-round turn fail outright (player_error after four retries), so her turn was silently skipped. Other players then read her silence as evasion: Carol said Mallory had 'twice now' declined to give a read when she had spoken only once. This set up the Day 1 suspicion thread against her. An infrastructure failure affected gameplay and was invisible to the players.

Day 3: Grace's answer was cut off at the output length limit (finish_reason length) and could not be parsed, so a retry was needed. The truncated private reasoning also appears in the error log. The output token budget seems too small for some players' answers.

Day 6: the program announced that speaking would start with Mallory, but Carol posted the first public message. Mallory may have passed silently, but the log does not record passes, so it is unclear whether turn order was followed.

Day 5, Ivan's trial: after posting his 'final word' public message, Ivan sent a private message to Mallory before the vote. R4 says the nominee gets 'one last public message before the vote' but does not say whether private messages are allowed after it. Earlier, Carol also sent a private message in the same turn she announced a nomination, before the nomination froze chat.

Day 4: Heidi argued that Clerk was 'a singleton' in Judy's archive sample and so must belong to one player. The Archivist shows only 7 of 10 roles at random, so that does not establish uniqueness (Dave pointed this out). Erin also cited R23 as the source of the swap-notification rule, but that notification is in the Smuggler role text, not R23.

Day 5: Ivan told Carol privately that 'Mallory's N5 result can test her claim tonight', but Ex-Con (Mallory's claimed role) gets no night result. This may have been deliberate misdirection by a Yakuza player, but it misstates the role's mechanics. Carol's Day 6 feedback also said the two-player trial math (both votes needed) should be stated more plainly.

Night 4 logging: Grace's Jester revenge got an explicit [Revenge] line, but Dave's Cardinal Divine Attack (which killed Frank) got no matching log line; it appears only as Frank's cause of death on Day 5. The [Night check] for Night 6 is also printed under the post-game debrief header. These are minor log-consistency gaps.
